scope: Offline analysis of retained actual current596 and peer558 traces, without a new profiler or benchmark run.
conclusion: No new high-share source-proven mathematical/resource/routing defect was found in the current BF16 decode. Projection matrix streaming is the dominant work in both arms. One genuine low-budget resource seam remains: GDN packed state is copied into the already distinct caller output page. Do not inflate it, kernel-count differences or software-profiler GraphLaunch intervals into a large wall-time claim.

kernel_counts.validation: All25 decode7..31 phases have these exact counts. 395 is peer nonprojection, not total. 596 vs395 was an apples-to-oranges count. Hyle has38 more physical kernels total,56 more nonprojection kernels, and18 fewer projection launches due to the a/b pair.
kernel_counts.logical_work: The same163 projection-role entries read the same matrices. Hyle18 a/b pairs each evaluate two logical MatMul values in one kernel, so physical145 does not mean less weight math.
kernel_counts.phase: decode7 is after the6th generated4B token D2H endpoint and through the7th; same named fixed-input phase in both retained traces.

comparison_contract.inputs: Same128 prompt tokens,31 forced decode input IDs and capacity256. Current trace target tape matches its current correctness/performance plan; peer trace was the latest retained matched peer capture. No free-generation token divergence is used to explain timing.
comparison_contract.precision: All observed projection matrices are BF16 in both. Hyle A/Y BF16 with F32 accumulation and explicit public BF16 rounding; peer native MMVF A/Y F32 with F32 accumulation, predominantly F32 pointwise intermediates. Same weights do not prove same intermediate mathematics or error.
comparison_contract.outputs: Both return a GPU-selected token to host. Peer additionally downloads248320 F32 logits (993280B) every phase, while current Hyle does not. The analysis retains both token-to-token intervals and a peer core interval beginning after the previous extra logits download. It does not silently delete that extra work from a benchmark wall-time number.
comparison_contract.capture: Both have one reused GraphLaunch per warm step. Current591 kernels are graph nodes and5 are eager; peer all558 are graph nodes. Physical graph node count also includes memcpy nodes and cannot be inferred from kernel count alone.
comparison_contract.time: These are distinct noncontemporaneous software-instrumented processes. Profiler diagnostics retain unsupported-driver fallback and software tracing notices. Neither frequency/power control nor exclusive GPU use is established. Phase minima/medians/ranges are attribution, not a speed comparison.

same_window_unprofiled.interpretation: Current median91.590 vs peer92.964 in this rotated window, with broad overlapping process ranges. This does not establish a stable1.5percent defect; historical larger gaps cannot be combined with current profile durations.

large_work.interpretation: Both arms spend about92percent of summed kernel elapsed time on projection carriers; gate/up, head and down alone account for75.19percent of logical matrix bytes. Current no-copy W views are dense row banks and remain BF16. No repeated hot projection weight widen/pack/CONT is present in the mapped current145 projection kernels.
large_work.not_a_bandwidth_counter: Bytes divided by kernel duration is nominal logical matrix throughput, not measured DRAM traffic. L2 reuse, repeated A loads, cache writeback and concurrent work require counters. No claim that all logical bytes hit DRAM each step.
